segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Hi, Dawn.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Oh hi, Ilmar.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: I’m glad I’ve bumped into you. I’ve just found a great idea for the presentation we’ve got to do for Dr Banks next month.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: What, the one on everyday objects?

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Yes ... look at this article ... it’s really interesting.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: The aluminium coke can?

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: You know ... coca cola cans, soft drink cans. Look let’s sit down here. Have you got a minute?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Sure ... I’ll just get my bag.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: OK, so you think we can get a presentation out of this article?

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: I’m sure we can. First of all we can provide some interesting facts about the aluminium cans that we drink out of every day.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Like ... ?

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Well, here ... it says that in the US they produce 300 million aluminium drink cans each day.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Wow! 300 million!

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Exactly. That’s an enormous number. It says here “outstrips the production of nails or paper clips”. And they say that the manufacturers of these cans exercise as much attention and precision in producing them as aircraft manufacturers do when they make the wing of an aircraft!

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Really! Let’s have a look.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: They’re trying to produce the perfect can - as thin but as strong as possible.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Mmm ... this bit’s interesting ... “today”s can weighs about 0.48 ounces: thinner than two pieces of paper ... from this magazine say.’

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Yeah, and yet it can take a lot of weight.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: More than 90 pounds of pressure per square inch — three times the pressure of a car tyre. OK, I agree, it’s a good topic.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: What I thought was that we could do a large picture of a coke can and label it and then talk about the different parts. Look, I’ve done a rough picture here.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: OK, so where shall we start?

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Well, the lid is complicated. Let’s start with the body first. I’ll do a line from the centre of the can ... like this ... and label it “body “. What does it say?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: It”s made of aluminium, of course, and it’s thicker at the bottom.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Right, so that it can take all that pressure.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: And then I think you should draw another line from the body for the label.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Right “label”. The aluminium is ironed out until it’s so thin that it produces what does it say?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: “A reflective surface suitable for decoration.”

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: That’s right apparently it helps advertisers, too.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Yes, because it’s so attractively decorated.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Good … and then there’s the base.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Yes, it says the bottom of the can is shaped like a dome so that it can resist the internal pressure.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: That’s interesting. I didn’t know that.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Nor did I. OK, so going up to the lid … there are several things we can label here. There’s the rim around the edge which seals the can.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Got that. And there’s a funny word for the seal isn’t there?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Yes, it’s a flange

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: What does it say about it?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Well, the can’s filled with coke or whatever and after that the top of the can is trimmed and then bent over to secure the lid.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: That’s right, it looks like a seam. We could even do a blow-up of it like this F-L-A-N-G-E ...

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Yes, that would be clearer. I think we should label the lid itself and say that it constitutes twenty five percent of the total weight.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Twenty-five percent … so it’s stronger than the body of the can.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: So to save money, manufacturers make it smaller than the rest of the can!

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Didn’t know that either ... so how do we open a can of coke?

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Mmm … first of all there’s the tab which we pull up to open the can and that’s held in place by a rivet.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: Mmm … I think that’s too small for us to include.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: I agree, but we can talk about it in the presentation. We can show the opening though

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: That’s the bit of the can that drops down into the drink when we pull the tab.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Yeah, hopefully. Sometimes the tab just breaks off.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: I know.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Anyway the opening is scored so that it pushes in easily but doesn’t detach itself.

segments.speaker: ILMAR
segments.en: OK, we can show that by drawing a shadow of it inside the can, like this I’ll label it scored opening. Great … well, I think we’ve got the basis of a really interesting presentation. Let’s go and photocopy the article.

segments.speaker: DAWN
segments.en: Fine. I’ll take it home and study it some more.
